gloss: to run out, to be exhausted

definitions.gloss: to run out, to be exhausted, to be used up
definitions.explanation: For a supply, resource, or abstract quality to be completely depleted or exhausted. Describes reaching the end of something finite.

examples.japanese: {体力|たいりょく}が{尽|つ}きた。
{食料|しょくりょう}が{尽|つ}きて{困|こま}っている。
examples.english: We're in trouble because the food supply has run out.

examples.japanese: {話題|わだい}が{尽|つ}きることなく、{朝|あさ}まで{語|かた}り{合|あ}った。
examples.english: Without running out of topics, we talked until morning.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
Often used in the pattern Xが{尽|つ}きる (X runs out). The negative form {尽|つ}きない and the pattern {尽|つ}きることなく (without running out) are common.

COLLOCATIONS:
- {体力|たいりょく}が{尽|つ}きる — stamina runs out
- {食料|しょくりょう}が{尽|つ}きる — food supply runs out
- {忍耐|にんたい}が{尽|つ}きる — patience runs out
- {話題|わだい}が{尽|つ}きない — topics never run out
- {言葉|ことば}に{尽|つ}きない — beyond words, inexpressible

SIMILAR WORDS:
なくなる is the everyday word for running out or disappearing. {尽|つ}きる is more literary and emphasizes complete exhaustion. {切|き}れる can also mean to run out (e.g., バッテリーが{切|き}れる) but focuses on breaking or disconnecting.
